title: Intel Rallies as Altera IPO Unlocks Its 49% Chip Stake
detail:
Intel Rallies as Altera IPO Unlocks Its 49% Chip Stake
Khac Phu Nguyen
Tue, September 15, 2026 at 8:34 AM MST 1 min read
INTC
Trade Intel on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Intel (NASDAQ:INTC), the processor designer and semiconductor manufacturer, rose approximately 2.2% to $99.32 Tuesday morning after Altera confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering. The move gives investors a new reason to focus on Intel's remaining stake in the programmable-chip business, which sells into data centers, AI infrastructure, telecommunications, industrial systems and defense markets.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with INTC.

Is INTC fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

INTC GF Value chart

Silver Lake bought 51% of Altera in September 2025, leaving Intel with a 49% holding. That stake could become much easier for investors to value once Altera reaches the public market. But the confidential filing leaves the biggest numbers unanswered: there is no disclosed share count, IPO price range or timetable yet. Until those details emerge, investors cannot reliably estimate either Altera's public valuation or the potential value of Intel's retained position.

Intel Rallies as Altera IPO Unlocks Its 49% Chip Stake · us.finance.gurufocus

The bigger test remains Intel itself. Second-quarter Data Center and AI revenue surged 59% to $6.3 billion, roughly 39% of total company revenue, while Intel still posted an $11 billion GAAP net loss partly driven by major charges. The valuation picture is already demanding: at $99.32, the shares sit 210.08% above the GuruFocus GF Value estimate of $32.03. That gap suggests investors are already pricing in a substantial operating recovery, making Altera's IPO a useful valuation catalystbut not a replacement for stronger profitability in Intel's core semiconductor business.

All three major US stock indexes were down in late-morning trading Tuesday, as Treasury yields continued to rise and investors increasingly expected the Federal Reserve to raise its benchmark interest rate at the conclusion of its two-day meeting on Wednesday.

In company news, Waystar (WAY) is considering multiple options, including a potential sale, Reuters reported Tuesday, citing seven sources familiar with the matter. The healthcare software company has hired Evercore (EVR) to advise on the process, the report said. Waystar shares were up 8.1% around midday. Evercore shares were down 2.1%.

Silver Lake- and Intel-backed (INTC) Altera said Tuesday its parent company has confidentially submitted a draft registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission relating to the proposed public offering of its common stock. Intel shares were up 1.1%.

Vera Therapeutics' (VERA) kidney disease treatment Trutakna achieved all prespecified endpoints during a final review of its Origin 3 study, with full US Food and Drug Administration approval expected in 2027, the drugmaker said Tuesday. Vera shares were down 1.9%.

Micron Technology (MU) is facing strike threats from a Taiwanese union representing company workers that is seeking a long-term transparent and verifiable profit-sharing mechanism instead of one-off rewards, Reuters reported Tuesday, citing the chairman of the union. Micron shares were up 0.7%.

General Motors (GM) said Tuesday it is launching a new user interface for pickup trucks featuring the latest versions of Apple (AAPL) CarPlay and Android Auto, with plans to deliver additional features and system enhancements through wireless software updates. The features will be available first in light-duty pickup trucks like the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and 2027 GMC Sierra before expanding across its broader portfolio, the company said. General Motors shares were down 2.1%.

As of 11:37 AM ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) is down 0.88% to 51,962, the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) has fallen 0.73% to 25,996, and the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) is trading 0.45% lower at 7,586 as concerns over high energy costs and AI scaling pressure indexes.

Gold is trading at $4,286.84, down 0.33%, while the 10-Year Treasury yield is up 0.03% to 4.99%. Sector-wise, communication stocks are the top gainer, with a sharp decline in industrials and weakness in consumer cyclicals.

Today's biggest moves

Nvidia, Intel, and Micron Technology all gained slightly this morning as investors reassessed doomsday scenarios for artificial intelligence (AI). Cryptocurrency stocks, including Coinbase Global and Robinhood Markets, dropped ahead of a Senate vote on key legislation.

What this means for investors

The 10-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2007 overnight, as the global bond sell-off resumed. High treasury yields, rising oil prices, and AI jitters all weighed on markets this morning as a cautious tone took hold. Markets are evaluating the potential impact of tightening economic conditions, particularly higher borrowing costs, on company earnings.

Although a couple of big tech stocks erased some of yesterday's losses, the Nasdaq still fell as fears of an AI slowdown were compounded by a growing certainty that the Federal Reserve will increase interest rates. AI warnings from tech leaders can be unnerving, but try to zoom out and look beyond the noise -- quality stocks with strong fundamentals and forecasts based on real demand will be well-positioned to withstand any short-term storms.

title: Intel-backed chipmaker Altera submits SEC paperwork for initial public offering
detail:
Intel-backed chipmaker Altera submits SEC paperwork for initial public offering
Luke Juricic
Tue, September 15, 2026 at 7:19 AM MST 1 min read
INTC
Trade Intel on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- Altera Corporation has confidentially submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a proposed initial public offering. The San Jose-based programmable chipmaker has not yet determined the number of common shares to be offered or the price range, with the timing remaining subject to regulatory review and prevailing market conditions.

The move initiates a fast-track return to public markets just one year after parent company Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC) carved out the unit, selling a 51% controlling stake to private equity firm Silver Lake in a transaction that valued Altera at $8.75 billion. Middle Eastern state fund MGX subsequently joined as a co-investor, while Intel retained a 49% minority holding to preserve upside from the business.

An offering would mark a pivotal step in establishing Altera as the largest pure-play provider of field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Known for chips that can be post-production reprogrammed to adapt to evolving computational demands, Altera is positioning its technology as a core building block for artificial intelligence infrastructure, industrial automation, robotics, and defense systems.

For Intel, the listing advances a broader corporate restructuring focused on shoring up liquidity and shedding non-core assets to fund its foundry turnaround. Intel originally acquired Altera in 2015 for approximately $16.7 billion, but later reversed course to grant the business operational autonomy amid rising capital demands across its core CPU and semiconductor manufacturing units.

title: MU Stock Rises After Micron Debuts 512GB DDR5 Server Memory – AMD, Intel To Validate New Server Technology
detail:
MU Stock Rises After Micron Debuts 512GB DDR5 Server Memory – AMD, Intel To Validate New Server Technology
Prabhjote Gill
Tue, September 15, 2026 at 7:23 AM MST 2 min read
MU
AMD
INTC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Micron expects the 512GB RDIMMs to enter volume production in the second half of 2027.

The company sees potential performance benefits for AI-related workloads, data analytics, databases and caching platforms.

AMD and Intel are validating the new memory technology for their respective server platforms.

Micron Technology (MU) shares rose in morning trade on Tuesday after the company announced it had demonstrated the first 512GB DDR5 registered dual in-line memory module (RDIMM) across multiple server platforms.

The company said its module can deliver speeds of up to 9,200 megatransfers per second (MT/s), while consuming more than 60% less operating power than four 128GB DDR5 modules.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

It added that Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Intel (INTC) are validating the memory for their server platforms. Their shares also rose in morning trade.

MU stock rose around 1.2% in morning trade, beating the broader market sell-off. INTC stock rose nearly 3%, and AMD stock gained around 3.5%.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around MU remained in 'bearish' territory over the past day, and sentiment around AMD stayed in the 'neutral' zone. Retail sentiment around INTC, meanwhile, dipped to 'bearish' from 'neutral' territory.

MU stock retail sentiment on September 15 as of 9:45 a.m. ET | Source: Stocktwits
Volume Production Planned for 2027

Micron said it expects the 512GB RDIMMs to enter volume production in the second half of 2027, subject to customer requirements. The company has not disclosed pricing or detailed availability timelines.

The memory is designed for data centers that handle large AI models, real-time inference, and high-core-count processors. It uses vertically stacked DRAM dies connected through through-silicon vias to increase memory density within individual packages.

A 24-slot, dual-socket server equipped with the modules could support up to 12 terabytes of DDR5 memory, according to Micron.

AMD, Intel Validate Micron's New RDIMM

Micron said AMD and Intel are validating the 512GB RDIMM for their server platforms. It added that the 512GB RDIMM can deliver up to 1.4 times the performance of 256GB DDR5 configurations in Spark support vector machine-based data analytics.

The company also cited potential gains in throughput and concurrency for databases and caching platforms such as RocksDB and Redis. However, Micron also noted that the performance gains will depend on the specific workload and server configuration.

MU stock has gained over 200% year-to-date and nearly 500% over the past 12 months amid the AI-boom in the stock market.

NVIDIA, AMD and Intel Forecast: AI Stocks Eye a Rebound
Christopher Lewis

INTC
NVDA
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
INTC Technical Analysis
Daily price chart for Intel showing shares trading near the 50-day EMA at $98.40. Source: TradingView

Intel is a little higher in pre-market trading, but recently we've seen some noise as broad semiconductor de-risking continues to be one of the stories here. Intel itself has been a fairly successful story over the last year as the turnaround continues for the company.

AI industry leaders got crushed. Perhaps the prospect of slowing frontier model development, as thrown out there by multiple leaders in the industry, has spooked the markets. Investors immediately figured that slower data-center CapEx and semiconductor demand would be part of that. It is a little overdone. It's just a few words, but it looks like the market is trying to turn things around.

Furthermore, you have to keep in mind that interest rates being higher than anticipated has been a bit of a drag.

NVDA Technical Analysis
Daily price chart for NVIDIA showing shares testing resistance near the 50-day EMA at $214.79. Source: TradingView

NVIDIA looks slightly positive in early market trading, with the market trying to reach toward the 50-day EMA. Again, this is about anxiety, with AI capital expenditures being the immediate problem. After all, if fewer data centers were to be built, NVIDIA is directly hit.

The market is looking at this in more fear-than-fact-based terms because NVIDIA's actual business numbers remain extraordinarily strong. So really, rates and the fear of a slowdown are fighting the reality of growth and economic numbers in this company that remain truly envy-worthy of most others.

AMD Technical Analysis
Daily price chart for AMD showing shares trading at $496.59 above the 50-day EMA. Source: TradingView

AMD looks slightly positive as well. The same situation applies as with NVIDIA. The question is, will there be less demand for chips? AMD's company-specific AI story remains exceptionally strong, like NVIDIA's, and they are expecting the addressable market to be approximately $2 trillion by 2030, so demand should still be out there.

It is increasingly landing major infrastructure deployments rather than simply presenting an alternative to NVIDIA. It is becoming a true competitor. The valuation is a bit high at the moment, but it looks like we are still very much in consolidation, with $450 offering a bit of a floor.
